newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shipyard, Solidarity birthplace, faces demise.
newsitem.headline: Polish shipyard, Solidarity birthplace, faces demise.

text.p: The bankrupt Gdansk shipyard, birthplace of the Solidarity movement that eventually toppled Poland's communist rulers, faced total collapse Wednesday after a bank refused to grant it a survival loan.
"The decision of the bank will probably make it necessary to terminate employment contracts with shipyard workers," PAP news agency quoted the yard's deputy receiver, Janusz Sledzinski, as saying.

There are still some 3,800 workers at the shipyard, which has operated under bankruptcy rules since last August, when its debts reached 415 million zlotys ($136 million) and banks refused further credit.

Earlier in the day, state-owned bank Pekao SA refused to extend a $100 million loan for the construction of five ships for a German shipowner, saying that terms of the prospective contract were unsatisfactory.
"In our opinion the deadlines for the construction of the ships are too optimistic and their budgets unrealistic," Pekao SA President Andrzej Dorosz told a news conference.

He said that under the contract the construction of the five ships would have to be done in eight or nine months, while the shipyard's track record showed it usually took 13 months to finish such jobs.
The receiver had hoped that the loan and the German contract would have kept at least part of the yard alive while he and the government sought an investor to save the business.
